name: Tactical Command Post

placement_rationale.text: 10.5 km sits directly on doctrine.md §2's own sourced figure for a combat-trains/rear command post (~10 km back from the line — the forward CP itself sits 2-5 km out, a depth this map already represents through the forward-sited squad and observation-post assets rather than duplicating here). Command posts are also deliberately dispersed from each other on this map's own lateral axis rather than clustered — concentrating C2 nodes is exactly the pattern that makes one lucky strike disproportionately costly, which is the opposite of the distributed-kill-chain shift doctrine.md §6 describes.

representative_system: Tactical/combat-trains command post — composite, not a specific named HQ

cost.display: Not a procurement item — a staffed position, not equipment

key_facts.label: Depth
key_facts.value: ~10 km back — doctrine.md's sourced combat-trains CP figure

key_facts.label: Function
key_facts.value: Directs the maneuver units and coordinates fires within its sector

key_facts.label: Survivability
key_facts.value: Dispersed from other C2 nodes rather than co-located, and relies on resilient comms

short_role: The maneuver-unit command post that actually directs the squads, guns and drone teams around it — distinct from the deep-rear sensor-fusion network node already on this map.
characteristics: Sits at doctrine.md's own sourced combat-trains-CP depth (~10 km), not the closer 2-5 km forward-CP figure this map represents through other forward-sited assets
Deliberately dispersed from other command posts and C2 nodes rather than co-located, to avoid one strike degrading the whole sector's command chain
Depends on resilient comms (including satellite links) the same way the deep-rear IADS network node does, just at a much shallower depth
Distinct from the existing c2-battle-management network asset, which is a rear sensor-fusion hub, not a maneuver command post
employment_notes: Represents a generic tactical/combat-trains command post directing a sector rather than a specific named headquarters. Positioned and dispersed per doctrine.md's own sourced depth figures rather than an assumed 'safe rear' distance.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional command posts could mass staff and communications equipment at one relatively fixed, well-protected location, trading concentration for coordination. Persistent drone ISR and precision strike make a concentrated C2 node a high-value, findable target, so the surviving pattern is smaller, more dispersed posts leaning on redundant, jam-resistant comms rather than one hardened bunker.

connections.description: Uses a resilient satellite link when terrestrial comms are jammed or cut.

notes: Written from doctrine.md and general knowledge; no per-asset citation yet.
